name: A Coruña
intro: Galicia's Atlantic port wraps around the UNESCO Torre de Hércules, the only Roman lighthouse still in service, with the world's longest urban seafront promenade (13 km), the wild Monte San Pedro overlooking the ocean, the Riazor and Orzán city beaches open to dogs October to May, and a 24/7 veterinary hospital on Calle Marqués de Amboage, one of Spain's most genuinely dog-friendly Atlantic bases.

name: Aarhus
intro: Denmark's second city, Scandinavia's most pet-tolerant café culture after Copenhagen. Free public transport for dogs, 8 official off-leash forests, year-round dog beaches at Bellevue Strand, and the iconic Den Gamle By open-air museum.

name: Aix-en-Provence
intro: Provence's elegant 17th-century university city, plane-tree-canopied Cours Mirabeau, baroque mansions, fountain-filled squares and the looming Sainte-Victoire painted by Cézanne. Compact, walkable, exceptionally dog-tolerant terraces and a 24/7 emergency vet on the Pont de l'Arc.

name: Ajaccio
intro: Corsica's sunlit capital and Napoléon's birthplace, a Genoese citadel on a sheltered gulf where year-round mild winters, Sentier des Crêtes ridge walks, the Sanguinaires boat tours and wild Capo di Feno dog beach make it Corsica's most pet-friendly base.

name: Albufeira
intro: The Algarve's largest beach resort, a city of two faces: the cobbled medieval Cidade Velha tumbling down to the fishermen's beach, and the busy resort strip of Areias de São João. Year-round dog beaches at Cova Redonda and Barranco das Belharucas, the Pine Cliffs clifftop trail in pine shade, and ~300 sunny days a year.

name: Alcúdia
intro: Alcúdia is a 21,000-resident town on the northern coast of Mallorca, defined by its intact 14th-century medieval walls with a 1.5 km perimeter walk around the casc antic, the Plaça de la Constitució with its Tuesday and Thursday morning market, the Església de Sant Jaume and Renaissance casas señoriales of Carrer Major, the 1st-century BC Pollentia Roman ruins (forum, residential quarter, theatre), the UNESCO Ramsar wetland of S'Albufera de Mallorca with 200+ bird species, the 6 km Platja d'Alcúdia (longest sandy beach on the island, Bandera Azul), the secluded Coll Baix pebble cove on Cap d'es Pinar, the cinematic Cap de Formentor lighthouse drive 30 km north, the 1-hour Iscomar fast catamaran from Port d'Alcúdia to Ciutadella de Menorca, and panadas de pix and rubiols as the signature Easter pastries.

name: Alicante
intro: Alicante is the sun-drenched capital of the Costa Blanca, a Mediterranean port crowned by the Castillo de Santa Bárbara with 320+ days of sunshine, the palm-lined Explanada de España, the year-round dog beach of Agua Amarga, and an easy TRAM north to Benidorm - one of Spain's most genuinely pet-friendly coastal bases.

name: Amsterdam
intro: Amsterdam is one of Europe's most dog-friendly cities, with parks, canals, and welcoming hotels.

name: Angers
intro: Angers, capital of the Anjou region in the Loire Valley, combines a 13th-century medieval fortress housing the world's largest medieval tapestry (the Apocalypse), a 700-hectare green network, and a 24/7 emergency vet, all within a 90-minute TGV from Paris.

name: Annecy
intro: Annecy, the 'Venice of the Alps', combines a UNESCO-rated medieval Vieille Ville on canals, the cleanest large lake in Europe, the 4 000-hectare Semnoz forest, and direct cross-border rail to Geneva (40 min).

name: Antibes
intro: Antibes pairs the Vauban ramparts, Provençal market and Cap d'Antibes coastal trail with a relaxed Côte d'Azur attitude to dogs on terraces, the Sentier de Tirepoil and the off-season Salis beach all welcome leashed dogs year-round.

name: Antwerp
intro: Antwerp's fashion-forward, dog-welcoming culture, riverside parks, and boutique hotel scene make it Belgium's most exciting city for pet travel.

name: Arles
intro: Arles is the southern terminus of the Provence Roman triangle: UNESCO amphitheatre, Théâtre Antique, Van Gogh sightlines and the Camargue wild beaches a short drive south. The official tourism office publishes a dedicated dog-travel page with leashing rules, vet contacts and ~30 dog-waste bag distributors across the historic centre.

name: Athens
intro: Athens surprises pet travellers: the city's mild climate means year-round outdoor dining, and many boutique hotels in Koukaki and Monastiraki actively welcome dogs. The Philopappos Hill parkland, with its panoramic views of the Acropolis, is just minutes from the historic centre.

name: Aveiro
intro: Aveiro, the 'Venice of Portugal', is a compact, flat and genuinely dog-friendly canal city, with three fenced municipal dog parks, broadly pet-tolerant esplanada terraces, traditional moliceiro boats that admit leashed dogs on request, and Atlantic dog beaches such as Cortegaca a short drive away.

name: Avignon
intro: Avignon, the Provençal capital and former seat of seven popes, combines a UNESCO-rated walled centro storico, the towering Palais des Papes, the legendary Pont Saint-Bénézet, and direct TGV access from Paris in 2h40.

name: Barcelona
intro: Barcelona has a growing pet-friendly scene with many hotels welcoming dogs of all sizes.

name: Bari
intro: Bari, the Adriatic capital of Puglia, pairs a walled medieval Old Town wrapped around the Basilica of San Nicola with Italy's longest seafront promenade and a network of dedicated off-leash dog parks opened since 2020. Three 24/7 vet hospitals, dog-friendly trattorie throughout Bari Vecchia, and easy train links to Polignano a Mare and Monopoli make it one of southern Italy's most underrated cities to travel with a pet.

name: Basel
intro: Basel sits at the corner of three countries, blending Swiss precision with a relaxed café culture and the Rhine running through its heart. Pet-friendly trams, two designated dog swim spots in the Rhine, off-leash forest walks along the Wiese river, and a 24/7 emergency vet clinic make it one of Europe's most underrated cities for travel with a dog.

name: Bath
intro: England's UNESCO Georgian spa town, honey-stone Royal Crescent, Roman baths, the 9.6 km Bath Skyline trail and the Kennet & Avon canal towpath. Compact, walkable, with a strong dog-tolerant pub culture and 24/7 emergency vet cover.

name: Bayonne
intro: Capital of the French Basque Country, at the confluence of the Nive and Adour rivers, with the red-shuttered half-timbered Vieux Bayonne, the 2.5 km Vauban rampart promenade, the UNESCO cathedral on the Camino de Santiago, and the Halles de Bayonne market. Compact pedestrian centre that crosses in 12 minutes on foot, jambon de Bayonne and Cazenave chocolate, and the dog-welcoming Petit Bayonne riverside quays.

name: Belfast
intro: Northern Ireland's revitalised capital on Belfast Lough, with the Cathedral Quarter pub scene, 750-acre Cave Hill Country Park rising directly above the city, the 18 km Lagan towpath, and year-round dog beaches on the County Down coast 20 minutes away. Strong British pub-and-dog culture, free dog travel on NI Railways, two 24/7 emergency vets.

name: Belgrade
intro: Belgrade is one of Europe's most affordable capitals, with the year-round Ada Ciganlija dog beach, dozens of fenced municipal dog parks, free public transport since 2025, and Serbia's only 24-hour vet hospital.

name: Bergamo
intro: Bergamo is one of northern Italy's most rewarding pet-friendly city breaks, a UNESCO-walled hilltop town with two pet-tolerant funiculars, the 4,700-hectare Parco dei Colli wrapping its northern flank, and Lake Iseo, Lake Como and Lake Garda all within an hour for cool dog-friendly day trips.

name: Bergen
intro: Norway's gateway to the fjords, wedged between seven mountains and the sea. Free public transport for dogs, off-leash mountains 7 minutes from the city centre, the UNESCO Bryggen wharf, and dog-tolerant café culture.

name: Berlin
intro: Berlin is one of the most dog-friendly capitals in Europe, with extensive parks and pet-welcoming accommodation.

name: Bern
intro: Bern is one of Europe's most pet-welcoming capitals, Switzerland's UNESCO Old Town has 6 km of covered Lauben arcades, three urban forests within tram distance, and the country's leading veterinary teaching hospital.

name: Béziers
intro: Béziers is a 78 000-resident Hérault city with the hilltop Cathédrale Saint-Nazaire perched 60 m above the Orb, the medieval Pont Vieux, the UNESCO Canal du Midi running directly through town with the spectacular Neuf Écluses de Fonsérannes 9-lock staircase, the Plateau des Poètes English landscape garden, and a 25 km Mediterranean sand corridor 15 minutes south anchored by the year-round off-leash Valras-Plage plage canine.

name: Biarritz
intro: Biarritz is a paradise for dogs and their owners, with beach access and pet-friendly hotels.

name: Bilbao
intro: Bilbao and the Basque Country rank among Spain's most dog-friendly destinations, where pintxos bars officially welcome dogs indoors and the tram accepts all sizes on a leash, the city's compact riverside design means a single walk connects the medieval Casco Viejo, Jeff Koons's 'Puppy' at the Guggenheim, and the dog-friendly Abandoibarra waterfront.

name: Bled
intro: Bled wraps a tiny alpine village around an emerald glacial lake with a 6 km dog-friendly shore circuit, the only island in Slovenia crowned by the Pilgrimage Church of the Assumption (reached by traditional pletna boats), an 11th-century clifftop castle that explicitly welcomes leashed dogs on its outdoor terraces, the wooden walkways of Vintgar Gorge, and direct gateway access to Triglav National Park, one of Europe's most naturally pet-friendly alpine bases.

name: Bologna
intro: Bologna's medieval porticoes and progressive urban fauna regulations make it Italy's most dog-welcoming city, dogs are legally permitted in all public premises, a 24/7 emergency vet operates inside the main park, and the UNESCO-listed Portico di San Luca offers a stunning shaded walk for any weather.

name: Bolzano
intro: Bolzano is the bilingual gateway to the Dolomites - half-Italian, half-Tyrolean, with vineyard walks, an 1890s panoramic promenade and a 12-minute cable car to the cool Renon plateau, all dog-friendly.

name: Bonn
intro: Bonn is Beethoven's birthplace, the post-war federal capital, and one of the greenest mid-sized cities in Germany - perfect for a Rhine-side dog weekend.

name: Bordeaux
intro: Bordeaux pairs world-class wine country with a relaxed, dog-friendly urban culture and excellent boutique hotels.

name: Boston
intro: Boston is New England's lakefront-and-harbour capital and the United States' oldest walkable city, where the distinctive Off-Leash Hours (OLH) program lets dogs run free dawn-to-09:00 in 20+ public parks (Boston Common at the head, the country's oldest public park, 1634), the 27 km Charles River Esplanade and the 4 km Freedom Trail provide the city's signature dog walking, and Peters Park in the South End is the only fully fenced off-leash dog park inside city limits. Castle Island/Pleasure Bay (off-season), the Arnold Arboretum and the Harborwalk welcome leashed dogs free of charge; the Seaport and Fort Point waterfronts run on the Massachusetts patio law (105 CMR 590.012). The MBTA T accepts small pets in carriers free and larger dogs off-peak at the operator's discretion (rare in the US); Amtrak's Acela out of South Station accepts small dogs for $26 per trip. Logan BOS is a CDC-approved international dog-arrival airport with indoor pet relief areas in every terminal. Angell Animal Medical Center in Jamaica Plain is one of the largest non-academic veterinary hospitals in the US. Mild springs and crisp autumns (April-June and September-November, 12-22 °C) are the prime dog seasons; harsh nor'easter winters (December-March, -10 to -15 °C with heavy pavement salt) demand paw protection.

name: Boulogne-sur-Mer
intro: Boulogne-sur-Mer is a 41 000-resident Pas-de-Calais Channel port (130 000 metro) that is France's largest fishing port by tonnage and home to Nausicaá, the largest aquarium in Europe. The walled Haute-Ville is encircled by the best-preserved 13th-century ramparts in France (1.5 km elevated chemin de ronde), the Cathédrale Notre-Dame crowns the upper town with a 101 m Italianate dome, the Cap d'Alprech lighthouse and chalk cliffs sit 3 km south, the GR120 coastal path runs north to Wimereux and Cap Gris-Nez, and direct TGV inOui links Boulogne-Ville to Paris Gare du Nord in 2h25.

name: Bournemouth
intro: Bournemouth is a south-coast English seaside resort with seven miles of golden sand, year-round dog-friendly beach zones at Fisherman's Walk and the Hengistbury end, a 2 km linear chain of public gardens through the centre, and the New Forest National Park half an hour north for off-leash forest hiking with free-roaming ponies to watch out for.

name: Braga
intro: Portugal's oldest city and youngest by student population, Braga pairs baroque heritage and Minho green hills with a famously pet-progressive café culture.

name: Brașov
intro: A medieval Saxon citadel at the foot of the Carpathian Mountains, Brașov pairs Transylvanian Gothic and pastel-painted squares with forested hiking trails and a notably dog-tolerant café scene on Piața Sfatului.

name: Bratislava
intro: Bratislava is a compact, affordable Central European capital where dogs walk the cobbled Old Town squares, the Carpathian forests of Železná Studnička, and the Danube embankments, all reachable on foot or one tram ride from the centre.

name: Bremen
intro: Bremen blends Hanseatic Old Town charm, the UNESCO Marktplatz with its Town Musicians and Roland statue, and 200 hectares of forested Bürgerpark right next to the centre, a perfect dog-friendly North German escape.

name: Brest
intro: Brest, Brittany's Atlantic naval port and largest city, anchors a deep natural harbour at the western tip of France, with the 50-hectare Vallon du Stang-Alar valley, the seafront Cours Dajot terrace, Penn ar Bed ferries to the Iroise islands and the dog-friendly GR34 coastal path linking the Pointe Saint-Mathieu, making it one of north-west France's most rewarding pet-friendly bases.

name: Brighton
intro: Brighton is the UK's most reliable seaside city for travelling with a dog: free buses, year-round dog beaches at Hove Lawns and Saltdean, dog-friendly cafés on every corner of The Lanes and Hove, and the South Downs National Park five kilometres from the centre.

name: Bristol
intro: One of England's most dog-friendly cities, 70% of pubs welcome dogs, free public transport for pets, the iconic Clifton Suspension Bridge, off-leash Downs and Ashton Court.

name: Brno
intro: Brno, Moravia's vibrant capital, combines a compact UNESCO-flanked old town, the Špilberk hilltop park, 14 fenced off-leash zones and a year-round dog-swimming reservoir 25 min away by tram.

name: Bruges
intro: Bruges, the UNESCO-listed medieval capital of West Flanders, combines a compact walkable centre, the 7 km tree-lined ramparts loop with four windmills, the Minnewater 'Lake of Love' park, the Belgian brown-café tradition that welcomes leashed dogs by default, and NMBS trains that carry dogs free to the Zeebrugge dog beach and Brussels.

name: Brussels
intro: Brussels punches above its weight as a pet travel destination: compact, walkable, with a café culture that extends happily to four-legged guests. The Bois de la Cambre and the vast Forêt de Soignes on the city's edge offer hours of off-lead woodland walking.

name: Bucharest
intro: Bucharest is one of the EU's most affordable capitals: 187-hectare Herastrau Park with two fenced municipal dog enclosures, Romania's largest 24/7 vet hospital, and Lake Snagov 40 km north for full-day forest swims.

name: Budapest
intro: Budapest's riverside parks, thermal bath culture, and affordable luxury hotels make it a rising star for pet-friendly travel in Eastern Europe.

name: Burgos
intro: Burgos crowns the Castilian plateau with its UNESCO Gothic cathedral, a key stop on the Camino de Santiago, eleven dog parks and easy riverside walks with your pet.

name: Cadaqués
intro: Cadaqués is a 2,800-resident pueblo blanco at the dead end of the GI-614 mountain road on the Cap de Creus headland, with a slate-paved old quarter piling up to the baroque Església de Santa Maria, the Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí complex in Port Lligat 1.5 km north of the centre (interior off-limits to pets, harbour and GR-92 path fine on a leash), Spain`s first marine-terrestrial Parc Natural at Cap de Creus, the easternmost mainland lighthouse Faro de Cap de Creus, and pebble coves at Cala Nans, Cala Jugadora, Cala Culip and Cala Sa Sabolla. There is no train station; access is by Sarfa/Moventis bus from Figueres (50 min) or by car on the GI-614, with the AVE high-speed rail terminating at Figueres-Vilafant 1 h west. The single in-village vet (Clínica Veterinària Cadaqués) refers overnight emergencies to Canis Hospital Veterinari in Figueres 35 km away. The tramuntana wind shapes the climate and the village`s identity.

name: Cadiz
intro: Cadiz pairs a compact, walkable old town with mild Atlantic weather and winter dog beaches: an easy Andalusian city break with your pet.

name: Caen
intro: Caen, the medieval Norman capital founded by William the Conqueror, combines a 1,000-year-old castle, two Romanesque abbeys, river and canal walks along the Orne, and easy day trips to the D-Day landing beaches 30 km west and the Bayeux Tapestry town.

name: Cagliari
intro: Cagliari, the Sardinian capital on the Mediterranean, combines a hilltop Castello quarter, 8 km of urban beach at Poetto with a seasonal dog stretch, a 1,600-ha flamingo lagoon, mild winters and a 24/7 reference vet hospital.

name: Calais
intro: Calais is a 67 000-resident Pas-de-Calais Channel ferry port facing the white cliffs of Dover, with 45 daily Dover crossings from P&O, DFDS and Irish Ferries, the pet-perfect Eurotunnel Le Shuttle from Coquelles where dogs stay in the car, the UNESCO Hôtel de Ville belfry and Rodin's Burghers of Calais, a 12 km Plage de Calais and Sangatte sand corridor, and the spectacular Grand Site Cap Blanc-Nez / Cap Gris-Nez chalk cliff trails 35 km west.

name: Calpe
intro: Costa Blanca centre town in Alicante province (24k residents), defined by the iconic 332 m Peñón de Ifach limestone monolith (Spain's smallest natural park, protected since 1987), the medieval casco antiguo with the Mudéjar Gothic Iglesia Antigua, the Las Salinas flamingo wetland in the middle of town, Roman Banys de la Reina archaeological pools, and the Bandera Azul Playa La Fossa-Levante (950 m of sand north of the Peñón). FGV TRAM narrow-gauge connections to Dénia, Benidorm and Alicante, 320 sunny days a year.

name: Cambridge
intro: Cambridge, England's iconic university city on the Cam, combines vast urban commons (Jesus Green, Midsummer, Coe Fen), riverside punting, and dog-tolerant historic pubs with direct 50-min train access from London King's Cross.

name: Cannes
intro: Cannes blends Riviera glamour with a surprisingly relaxed dog culture, terraces along Le Suquet, the Marché Forville, and the western beaches all welcome four-legged guests year-round.

name: Capri
intro: Capri, the storied limestone island in the Bay of Naples, pairs panoramic clifftop walks with a calm pet-friendly base in upper Anacapri, the year-round Via Krupp and Punta Tragara paths to the Faraglioni, and reliable garden-terrace dining; ferries from Naples and Sorrento accept leashed dogs and the day-trip-or-overnight choice is the key decision for pet travellers.

name: Carcassonne
intro: The largest medieval walled city in Europe, where leashed dogs roam 3 km of double ramparts, 52 towers and the outer courtyards of Château Comtal, with the Canal du Midi towpath and Lac de la Cavayère shoreline for swimming and shade.

name: Cardiff
intro: The Welsh capital pairs a 130-hectare riverside park network with a compact dog-welcoming city centre, a 2 km Cardiff Bay barrage walk linking directly to Penarth Pier, and a 24/7 reference emergency hospital fifteen minutes north.

name: Cascais
intro: Cascais, Lisbon's elegant coastal escape, combines a marina-fronted old town with abundant dog-friendly terraces, the eighteen-hectare Parque Marechal Carmona, the three-kilometre Paredão promenade to Estoril, the dramatic Boca do Inferno cliff walk, and the wild Atlantic dune beaches of the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park.

name: Catania
intro: Catania, Sicily's lava-built Baroque capital under the slopes of Mount Etna, pairs a UNESCO-listed historic centre with a dedicated municipal dog beach, three 24/7 vet hospitals and one of the densest pet-friendly café cultures in southern Italy. Dogs ride free in carriers on the Trenitalia regional trains to Taormina, walk the cool Pescheria fish market at dawn, and shelter in the Norman pines of Villa Bellini.

name: Český Krumlov
intro: Český Krumlov, a UNESCO World Heritage town of 13 000 residents in the Bohemian Forest foothills, packs Czech Republic's second-largest castle complex, painted Renaissance lanes and a tight Vltava-river bend into a 15-minute walking circle. Dogs on a short leash are welcome on the castle's five outer courtyards and the iconic Cloak Bridge, in the Baroque Castle Garden (April–October), and on the riverside promenades - though indoor museum sections, the Round Tower climb and rafting boats remain off-limits. The closest 24-hour vet is 25 km north in České Budějovice.

name: Chania
intro: Crete's western capital (~110k), gateway to the Venetian Old Town, Souda port ferries and the most spectacular beaches in Greece (Falassarna, Elafonissi, Balos). A Venetian-Ottoman harbour ringed by Splantzia alleys, the Egyptian Lighthouse breakwater, and the Firkas Fortress. Arguably the most dog-friendly Greek city, with year-round mild climate, off-season dog beach at Nea Chora, and bilingual EL/EN vets. 1h flight from Athens; direct from most EU hubs in summer; 9h overnight ferry from Piraeus.

name: Chicago
intro: Chicago is the Midwest's lakefront capital, where one of the largest US Dog Friendly Area (DFA) networks (25+ fenced off-leash parks plus the dedicated Montrose Dog Beach, the only off-leash beach in the city) combines with a flat 29 km Lakefront Trail along Lake Michigan, the 485-hectare Lincoln Park anchoring the North Side, and the free Lincoln Park Zoo's perimeter paths. Millennium Park's Cloud Gate ('The Bean') and Crown Fountain, the 2 km Chicago Riverwalk, Maggie Daley Park and Grant Park welcome leashed dogs free of charge; Wrigleyville's game-day bar patios run on the Illinois patio law (Public Act 99-0937). CTA 'L' trains, buses and Metra commuter rail all accept small pets in carriers free; O'Hare (ORD) is a CDC-approved international dog-arrival airport with indoor pet relief areas in every terminal. Two solid in-city 24/7 emergency vets (MedVet Chicago, Premier Veterinary Group) cover the metro. Hot humid summers (June-August, 25-32 °C) and crisp falls are the prime dog seasons; brutal winters (December-March, -10 to -20 °C windchill with lake-effect snow) demand paw protection and short walks.

name: Ciutadella de Menorca
intro: Menorca's former capital sits on the wild west coast of the island, a honey-coloured Italianate old town around the Plaça d'es Born and the 14th-century Gothic cathedral, with the 5 km Camí de Cavalls GR-223 coastal trail starting from the Castell de Sant Nicolau lighthouse, the UNESCO Talaiotic Naveta des Tudons megalith 4 km east, the most photographed coves of Menorca (Cala Macarella, Cala Macarelleta, Cala en Turqueta) 15 km south, the 1-hour fast catamaran ferry to Alcúdia on Mallorca, and 24-hour vet emergency cover referred to Clínica Veterinaria Cardona & von Hofe in Mahón (608 53 43 43).

name: Coimbra
intro: Portugal's third city and its medieval capital (1131–1255), home to the UNESCO-listed University of Coimbra (founded 1290, one of Europe's oldest). The hilltop old town tumbles down to the Mondego river in narrow lanes and stairways. 1h45 from Lisbon and 1h15 from Porto by Alfa Pendular train. Spring and autumn are ideal; summers are warm (28–30°C) but breezy.

name: Cologne
intro: Cologne (Köln) sits on the Rhine with its iconic cathedral and a vibrant dog culture, the KVB city network welcomes dogs in carriers and the vast Stadtwald forest offers one of western Germany's best off-leash walking experiences.

name: Como
intro: Como sits at the southern tip of Lake Como with the Alps rising behind, a luxury lakeside town where pet-friendly ferries cross to Bellagio and Varenna, the Brunate funicular climbs to dog-welcome panoramas, and Villa Olmo's lakeshore gardens are open to leashed dogs year-round.

name: Copenhagen
intro: Copenhagen leads Europe in sustainability and pet-friendliness: dogs are welcomed in shops, restaurants, and on public transport.

name: Cordoba
intro: Andalusia's UNESCO Mezquita-Catedral city, 45 min by AVE from Seville. Compact whitewashed historic centre, the famous Roman Bridge over the Guadalquivir, and the Sierra Morena foothills 15 min north for cool dog hikes. Spring and autumn are the dog-trip seasons; summer hits 40 C+.

name: Corfu
intro: Corfu (Kerkyra, ~25k in the capital, ~100k island-wide) is the Ionian gateway where a UNESCO-listed Venetian Old Town layers 400 years of Venetian rule, French Napoleonic arcades (the Liston) and British neoclassical palaces (St Michael and St George). The 8-hectare Spianada is the largest public square in Greece, the Old Fortress promontory offers a 360 degree harbour panorama, the Mon Repos villa park (Prince Philip's birthplace) gives the shadiest in-town dog walk, and Kanoni's Pontikonisi Mouse Island view is the island's iconic postcard. Beaches range from the urban Garitsa Bay (10 min walk) to Glyfada 17 km west, the cove cluster of Paleokastritsa 25 km NW, and the sandstone Canal d'Amour at Sidari. Lush green and milder than the Aegean thanks to the Ionian climate; ideal Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct. CFU airport is only 2 km south of the centre; the New Port runs hourly Igoumenitsa ferries (1h30) and overnight Brindisi/Bari ferries to Italy.

name: Cork
intro: Cork, Ireland's foodie capital and rebel city, wraps the River Lee with Georgian streets, snug-friendly pubs and the 200-hectare Ballincollig off-leash park, with Cork Harbour beaches a 25-minute drive away.

name: Dénia
intro: Costa Blanca north port city, UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy, 11th-century Moorish Castillo above the casco antiguo, the 753 m Montgó Natural Park rising directly behind town, and the Platja Canina de Les Deveses year-round dog beach. Daily Baleària ferries to Ibiza, Mallorca and Formentera. 320 sunny days a year.

name: Dresden
intro: Dresden combines a compact baroque centre with kilometres of off-leash Elbe meadows and a 5,800-hectare municipal forest, making it one of eastern Germany's easiest cities for travellers with a dog.

name: Dublin
intro: Dublin's pub gardens, Phoenix Park, and warm Irish welcome extend to dogs: making it one of the most dog-friendly capitals in Europe.

name: Dubrovnik
intro: Dubrovnik's dramatic coastline, island day-trips, and boutique hotels outside the Old Town walls offer a memorable setting for pet owners.

name: Dunkerque
intro: Dunkerque is an 86 000-resident Nord Channel port (200 000 metro) that is France's third-largest port and the gateway to the DFDS Dunkerque-Dover ferry crossing. The UNESCO Beffroi Saint-Éloi crowns the centre, the Mémorial Operation Dynamo and Mémorial du Souvenir trace the 1940 evacuation of 338 000 Allied troops, the 12 km dune coast from Malo-les-Bains to Bray-Dunes at the Belgian border is the longest continuous coastal dune walk on the French Channel coast, the DK'Bus citywide network is 100% free for everyone since 2018, and the Carnaval de Dunkerque fills the city six weekends in February-March.

name: Düsseldorf
intro: Düsseldorf pairs Rhineland brewpub culture with one of Germany's most extensive park networks, 21 official off-leash Hundewiesen, Frank Gehry's Medienhafen waterfront, and Unterbacher See's lake-bathing zones 20 minutes south of the centre.

name: Edinburgh
intro: Edinburgh's dramatic hills, Arthur's Seat, and deeply dog-welcoming pub culture make it one of Britain's best cities for a break with your dog.

name: Ericeira
intro: Ericeira, Europe's only World Surfing Reserve 40 km north of Lisboa, pairs a clifftop old town above Praia dos Pescadores with the Ribeira d`Ilhas WSL Championship Tour break, the Coxos right-hand reef, dog-tolerant marisqueira terraces and the monumental Palácio Nacional de Mafra and 800-hectare Tapada royal forest 10 km inland.

name: Évora
intro: Évora, the Alentejano UNESCO capital and former Roman, Visigoth and Moorish town, combines a 2,000-year-old Roman Temple, the eerie Capela dos Ossos (Bone Chapel), one of Iberia's largest medieval city wall circuits, and direct CP rail access from Lisbon in 1h30.

name: Faro
intro: Faro, the Algarve capital and gateway to Portugal's southern coast, combines a UNESCO-rated medieval Cidade Velha, the 18,000-hectare Ria Formosa Natural Park with year-round flamingo boardwalks, dog-friendly Atlantic barrier-island beaches via ferry, and direct international flights from across northern Europe.

name: Florence
intro: Florence's Renaissance beauty is matched by a surprisingly welcoming attitude toward dogs: in restaurants, on the Arno riverbanks, and in the Boboli gardens.

name: Formentera
intro: Formentera is the smallest of the four major Balearic Islands, a flat 19 km strip of pale sand, juniper scrub and UNESCO-protected Posidonia seagrass meadows reachable only by ferry from Ibiza (30-45 min). 12,000 permanent residents swell to nearly 70,000 in peak summer; the rest of the year it is one of the calmest dog walks in the Mediterranean. Ses Illetes beach is regularly voted Europe's best, two clifftop lighthouses anchor the eastern and southern tips, and leashed dogs are welcome on the Camí Romà path to La Mola plateau. The seasonal beach ban runs 1 June-30 September, so April-May and October-November are the sweet spot. Access: Balearia, Aquabus and Trasmapi ferries from Ibiza Town port to La Savina.

name: Frankfurt
intro: Germany's financial capital is also one of its greenest, 52% of the city is woodland, parks, or water. With dog-friendly Sachsenhausen taverns, the 4,200-hectare Stadtwald, and two 24/7 emergency vet clinics, Frankfurt is a reliable stop on any European pet road trip.

name: Freiburg im Breisgau
intro: A 236,000-resident Baden city at the foot of the Black Forest and Germany's sunniest urban centre. The pedestrian Altstadt with its famous Bächle water channels, the Gothic Münster, the Schauinslandbahn cable car up to the 1,284 m mountain and the off-leash forest trails of the Schwarzwald combine in one of the most dog-tolerant eco-cities in Europe.

name: Fréjus
intro: Fréjus is the most dog-friendly municipality on the French Riviera by a clear margin: three official year-round dog beaches, a 100-hectare Base Nature park with a brand-new enclosed Woof Park, dogs admitted at the Roman amphitheatre, and the red rocks of the Massif de l'Estérel as a coastal hiking backdrop.

name: Funchal
intro: The capital of Madeira sits in a south-facing volcanic amphitheatre with year-round mild Atlantic weather, miles of dog-friendly esplanadas, the cliff-side Lido promenade, and the only 24/7 veterinary hospital on the island. Levada walks above town and pebble coves at Caniço round out one of the most reliably pet-friendly winter destinations in Europe.

name: Galway
intro: Galway's bohemian Latin Quarter, Atlantic beaches, and pub-centred culture extend a famously warm welcome to dogs along the Wild Atlantic Way.

name: Gdansk
intro: Gdansk, the Hanseatic Pearl of the Baltic and former Free City of Danzig, combines a UNESCO-rated Długi Targ, the Solidarity birthplace at Stocznia Gdańska, and direct SKM rail access to Sopot Dog Beach (the most famous in Poland) in 15 minutes.

name: Gdynia
intro: Gdynia, the modernist port half of Poland's Tricity (with Gdansk and Sopot), 244 000 residents, two year-round dedicated dog beaches (Orlowo and Kolibki with agility), two 24-hour emergency vets, the Sea Towers, the South Pier museum ships (Dar Pomorza, ORP Blyskawica), and direct SKM rail to Sopot Dog Beach in 15 minutes.

name: Geneva
intro: Geneva is one of Europe's most pet-welcoming international capitals, Swiss law allows dogs in restaurants and cafés, the Bois de la Bâtie offers year-round off-leash forest, and two 24/7 emergency vet centres serve the city.

name: Genoa
intro: Genoa is one of Italy's most quietly pet-welcoming cities, the first in Liguria to open an official dog beach, with three urban green parks, the historic Strade Nuove UNESCO district, and 24/7 emergency vet clinics on call.

name: Getxo
intro: Bilbao's coastal neighbour on the Bay of Biscay, 78k inhabitants, home of the UNESCO Vizcaya Bridge (Puente Colgante, the world's first transporter bridge, 1893, dog-friendly since 2017), the picturesque Puerto Viejo de Algorta with its stepped pintxo plazas, the 6 km Punta Galea cliff path from the 18th-century Aixerrota windmill to Sopelana, and 17 designated off-leash dog-recreation zones. Three urban beaches (Ereaga, Las Arenas, Arrigunaga) closed to dogs as recreation 1 May to 30 September.

name: Ghent
intro: Ghent, the UNESCO-listed Flemish university capital of East Flanders, combines Europe's largest car-free historic centre, the 12th-century Gravensteen castle of the Counts of Flanders, Van Eyck's Mystic Lamb at Saint Bavo's Cathedral, the medieval Graslei-Korenlei quays on the Leie, the Citadelpark with a fenced off-leash zone, the Blaarmeersen in-city dog beach, and NMBS trains that carry dogs free to Bruges in 25 min and Brussels in 30 min.

name: Glasgow
intro: Glasgow is among the UK's most reliably dog-friendly cities: free pets on every ScotRail train, dog-welcoming pubs in every neighbourhood, the 146-hectare Pollok Country Park inside the city, and Loch Lomond a 50-minute train ride away.

name: Gothenburg
intro: Gothenburg is Sweden's most dog-friendly city, a lively port city with vast urban forests, dog-welcoming café culture, and a Scandinavian transit system that treats pets as first-class passengers.

name: Graz
intro: Austria's second city and capital of Styria, with the largest preserved Renaissance and Baroque old town in Central Europe, UNESCO-listed since 1999. The Schlossberg hill with its iconic Uhrturm clock tower dominates a compact, walkable centre crossed by the Mur river. 2h30 from Vienna by Railjet. A young, green university city with strong pet culture and easy access to Styrian forests and lakes.

name: Guimarães
intro: Guimarães, the UNESCO-listed birthplace of Portugal, packs a 10th-century granite castle, the 15th-century Paço dos Duques palace, the iconic Largo da Oliveira medieval square and the Penha mountain reached by Portugal's longest cable car into a compact, fully pedestrianised old town. The Minho climate stays pet-friendly from April through October and 24/7 vet cover anchors every itinerary.

name: Haarlem
intro: Haarlem is the Netherlands' most painlessly dog-friendly base for the Amsterdam region: a compact medieval city 20 km west of Amsterdam where the Grote Markt under the Grote Sint-Bavokerk (Frans Hals's tomb, the 1766 Mozart Müller organ), the Frans Hals Museum, the Teylers Museum (the oldest in the country), the Spaarne river with the De Adriaan windmill, and a network of sixteen historic almshouse courtyards (hofjes) cluster inside the singel canals. Haarlemmerhout is the oldest public park in the Netherlands (1583); the Schoterbos has two off-leash dog meadows. The Zandvoort dog beach is 10 minutes by NS train (year-round at Zandvoort Zuid hondenstrand, off-leash on the full 9 km from October 1 to May 1), Bloemendaal aan Zee 15 minutes by bus, and the 38 km² Nationaal Park Zuid-Kennemerland 6 km west. NS IC trains reach Amsterdam Centraal in 15 minutes every 10 minutes (dogs in carrier free, larger dogs €3.30 Dagkaart Hond); Schiphol Airport is a 20-minute direct Sprinter; Connexxion R-Net buses serve the dunes and beach.

name: Hallstatt
intro: Hallstatt is the UNESCO World Heritage lakeside village of the Salzkammergut, a 750-resident Alpine icon where dogs walk the lake promenade, ride the funicular and the boat for free, and explore the dog-friendly Echerntal valley and Gosausee trails.

name: Hamburg
intro: Germany's second-largest city and one of its most dog-friendly, 14% green space, 56 fenced off-leash zones, a 7 km Alster lake walking loop, the famous Elbstrand urban beaches and two 24/7 emergency vet clinics. A port culture with deep roots and wide horizons.

name: Hannover
intro: Lower Saxony's capital, Germany's largest urban forest (Eilenriede, 640 ha), the Maschsee lake with its dog swim zone, the baroque Herrenhäuser Gärten, and a world-class veterinary university hospital. One of the calmest German big-city bases for dog owners.

name: Heidelberg
intro: Heidelberg, Germany's most romantic university city, combines a baroque Altstadt under the ruined Renaissance castle, the iconic Philosophenweg view path, the Königstuhl forest with 70 km of off-leash trails, and direct ICE trains from Frankfurt Airport in 50 minutes.

name: Helsinki
intro: Helsinki's island archipelago, its love of outdoor life, and its exceptionally clean air make it one of Northern Europe's finest pet travel destinations. Dogs are welcomed on city ferries, in many cafés, and across the Nuuksio national park trails just 35km from the city centre.

name: Heraklion
intro: Crete's capital and largest city (~145k), gateway to the Minoan palace of Knossos (4 km south) and ferry hub for the eastern Mediterranean. Massive 16th-century Venetian walls ring a lively centre of tavernas, the harbour fortress Koules, and the Heraklion Archaeological Museum. The dog-friendliest of Greek major cities thanks to the year-round mild climate, several signed Bau-Beach zones east of town, and a relaxed Cretan attitude toward pets on terraces. 1h flight from Athens; direct from most EU hubs.

name: Hvar
intro: Hvar is the Dalmatian `sun island` (2,718 sun hours a year, the most in Croatia) - 11,000 residents island-wide, 3,700 in tiny Hvar Town clustered around Saint Stephen`s Square (the largest piazza in Dalmatia), the 16th-century cathedral, the 1612 Arsenal theatre, the cliff-clinging Franciscan Monastery and the Fortica Španjola fortress on the hill behind, with the Pakleni Islands archipelago strung off the western tip (water-taxis from the harbour year-round, dogs welcome on most boats and on Palmižana/Mlini bays), Stari Grad 20 km east (the oldest town in Croatia, founded as Greek Pharos 384 BC, with its UNESCO-listed agricultural plain), lavender ridges around Velo Grablje, and Plavac Mali vineyards on the steep south coast at Sveta Nedjelja. No airport on Hvar: access is by Jadrolinija fast catamaran from Split (SPU 2 h door-to-door) to Hvar Town in 1 h, or by Jadrolinija/Krilo car ferry from Split to Stari Grad in 1 h 45.

name: Hyères
intro: Hyères-les-Palmiers is one of the few French Riviera resorts with an official year-round dog beach (Plage du Mérou), a 24/7 on-site vet clinic and the Giens tombolo salt flats and Porquerolles ferry as dog-accessible day trips.

name: Ibiza
intro: Capital of the Balearic island of Eivissa, Ibiza Town wraps around a UNESCO-listed walled old town (Dalt Vila), a pine-forested interior, and one of Europe's most surprisingly dog-relaxing shoulder seasons. Beyond the clubbing cliché, year-round residents walk dogs through Sa Penya and the harbour, a handful of beaches (Cala Bassa, Cala Nova) tolerate dogs out of summer ban (15 May–15 October), and the ferry to Formentera opens a calmer second island for canine day trips. Direct flights from most EU hubs to Ibiza Airport (IBZ).

name: Innsbruck
intro: Tyrol's capital encircled by 2,300m Alpine peaks. Free public transport for dogs, dog-friendly cable cars to mountain summits, café and Gasthaus tradition that welcomes dogs, and 24/7 emergency vet. The signature Alpine pet-travel base.

name: Interlaken
intro: Switzerland's Jungfrau Region gateway sits on the Bödeli between Lakes Thun and Brienz, with the 10-hectare Höhematte meadow framed by Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, the Harder Kulm funicular for muzzled dogs at 1322 m, dog-friendly BLS heritage paddle steamers on both lakes, leashed-and-muzzled access on most Jungfraubahn lines (with altitude limits above Eigergletscher 2320 m), and a verified 24/7 vet line at Tierklinik Interlaken AG.

name: Jurmala
intro: Jurmala, Latvia's most famous beach resort, 33 km of white-sand Baltic coast 30 minutes by train from Riga, wooden Art Nouveau dachas of Dzintari and Majori, the Dubulti viewpoint, and the only Baltic resort where leashed dogs get a full 33 km of empty winter beach from November to March.

name: Kaunas
intro: Kaunas, Lithuania's interwar capital from 1919 to 1939, is built around the 1.6 km Laisvės alėja pedestrian boulevard and 1,500 UNESCO-inscribed Modernist buildings (2023 World Heritage listing), with the Baroque Pažaislis Monastery on the Kaunas Lagoon, 63 hectares of mature oak grove at Ąžuolynas, dog-friendly buses and trolleybuses, and two 24/7 emergency vets.

name: Klagenfurt am Wörthersee
intro: A 104,000-resident Carinthian capital on the eastern shore of the Wörthersee, the warmest lake in the Alps (up to 26 degrees in July). The Renaissance Altstadt with its iconic Lindwurmbrunnen dragon fountain, the Minimundus miniature park, the Kreuzbergl forest above the city and several signed Hundebadeplätze on the lake make it one of Austria's most relaxed dog-travel bases.

name: Klaipeda
intro: Klaipeda is Lithuania's only Baltic port and the gateway to the UNESCO Curonian Spit, a compact 150,000-resident city where the free Smiltyne ferry takes dogs over to pine forest and white-sand beach in 5 minutes, the Old Town packs Memel-era timber houses, Theatre Square and a 12-hectare Sculpture Park, and a 24/7 referral veterinary hospital backs every itinerary.

name: Krakow
intro: Krakow's magnificent medieval Rynek (Market Square) is ringed by leafy streets that are surprisingly dog-friendly, and hotels here are among Poland's most welcoming to pets. The Planty park: a 4km ring of greenery encircling the old town: is ideal for early-morning walks before the tourist crowds arrive.

name: Lagos
intro: Lagos in the western Algarve combines a 16th-century walled old town, the ochre limestone cliffs of Ponta da Piedade with a 4 km dog-friendly clifftop boardwalk, the 4 km Meia Praia dune (one of Portugal's best off-season dog beaches), the year-round dog zone at Praia de Porto de Mós, and a mild oceanic climate that stays pet-friendly from October through May.

name: Lausanne
intro: Lausanne is one of Europe's most dog-welcoming cities, Switzerland's Olympic Capital on Lake Geneva where dogs are permitted in restaurants, on public transport, and even in some museums.

name: Lecce
intro: Lecce, the 'Florence of the South', combines a UNESCO baroque centro storico, dog-tolerant Salento café culture, year-round dog beaches at Punta Prosciutto and Frassanito 30-45 minutes away, and prices well below central Italy.

name: Leipzig
intro: Leipzig, Saxony's musical capital and the city of Bach, combines the 5,500-hectare Auenwald floodplain forest, the dog-friendly Karl-Heine-Kanal towpath, 11 fenced Hundeauslaufzonen, and a year-round Hundestrand at Cospudener See 12 minutes by S-Bahn.

name: Liepaja
intro: Liepaja, Latvia's third largest city and main southern Baltic port, the city where the wind is born, with a 7 km Blue Flag beach, the largest unreconstructed mechanical organ in the world, and the only military prison in Europe you can spend the night in.

name: Lille
intro: Lille is northern France's flemish-influenced capital, a flat, walkable city of cobbled lanes and brick gabled houses where dogs join their owners on café terraces, ride the métro free, and explore Europe's first dedicated dog café.

name: Linz
intro: Linz is Austria's third-largest city and an under-rated dog-travel destination: a compact baroque Altstadt on the Danube, an off-leash zone with river swimming for dogs, a 539 m forested hill reached by Europe's steepest adhesion railway, and a tram network that carries dogs free on every monthly ticket.

name: Lisbon
intro: Lisbon's mild climate and relaxed culture make it ideal for travelling with your pet.

name: Liverpool
intro: Liverpool pairs UNESCO-listed waterfront grandeur with one of north-west England's largest urban park networks, three off-leash dog beaches within 25 minutes by Merseyrail, and a Baltic Triangle pub corridor that welcomes leashed dogs year-round.

name: Ljubljana
intro: Ljubljana: Europe's green capital: is one of the continent's most walkable, bike-friendly, and dog-welcoming small cities.

name: London
intro: With nearly half of households owning a dog and hundreds of dog-welcoming pubs and parks, London is one of Europe's most naturally pet-friendly capitals, from Hyde Park's off-leash zones to Bermondsey's dog-friendly restaurant strip.

name: Los Angeles
intro: Los Angeles is California's Pacific entertainment capital, where Griffith Park's 1700-hectare urban wilderness with the Observatory terrace, Runyon Canyon's off-leash Hollywood Hills trails, the Silver Lake Reservoir Dog Park, the Venice Boardwalk and Abbot Kinney, the Santa Monica Pier and the Getty Center exterior gardens anchor a year-round Mediterranean outdoor lifestyle uniquely friendly to dogs. Rosie's Dog Beach in Long Beach is the only legal off-leash beach in LA County; Leo Carrillo in Malibu (leashed) and Huntington Dog Beach in Orange County (off-leash) sit within an hour. LA Metro Rail and Metro Bus admit small pets in carriers, the Amtrak Pacific Surfliner accepts pets up to 20 lb along the coast, LAX is a CDC-approved dog-import gateway with eight indoor pet relief areas, and 24/7 emergency vet care is dense across the metro. Peak season runs October to May; June to September brings 50-55 °C asphalt heat in the inland valleys that limits midday walking.

name: Lucca
intro: Tuscany's perfectly preserved walled city, 4.2 km of Renaissance ramparts (1545-1650) ring an intact medieval centre with the oval Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, the Guinigi Tower with oak trees growing on its roof, and the Romanesque-Pisan Duomo. ~89k inhabitants, 30 min by train from Pisa and 80 min from Florence. The walls are a paved 4 km dog-walking loop on grass, Italy's flagship Renaissance walking promenade.

name: Lucerne
intro: Lucerne combines a UNESCO-listed lake setting, dog-friendly cogwheel mountains and Switzerland's most relaxed terrace culture for a perfect Swiss city break with a dog.

name: Lugano
intro: Lugano is the elegant Italian-speaking face of Switzerland - a 63,000-resident lakeside city of palms, porticoes and Lombard architecture where dogs ride the boat for free, swim at Caslano's dog beach, and walk the Sentiero dell'Olivo to Gandria.

name: Luxembourg
intro: Luxembourg has free public transport for everyone (including dogs) since 2020, nine fenced municipal dog enclosures inside the city, two 24-hour vet clinics, and a UNESCO Old Town with leash-friendly fortification walks above the Pétrusse and Alzette river valleys.

name: Lyon
intro: Lyon's gastronomic culture extends to its terrace restaurants and bouchons, many of which welcome well-behaved dogs.

name: Maastricht
intro: Maastricht, the Netherlands' oldest city and Limburg's Burgundian capital, combines a compact medieval centre, the Sint-Pietersberg forest hill, 22 fenced losloopgebieden, and walkable triple-frontier access to Belgium and Germany.

name: Madrid
intro: Madrid is one of Europe's most dog-friendly capitals, with sprawling parks, dog-welcoming terraces, and a thriving pet culture.

name: Mahón
intro: Menorca's whitewashed capital sits at the head of the world's second longest natural deep-water harbour after Pearl Harbor, with the 5 km Moll de Llevant promenade walking dogs along the Port de Maó, the UNESCO Talaiotic Bronze Age megaliths at Trepucó on the city outskirts, the 185 km Camí de Cavalls coastal trail circling the island for leash-friendly multi-day hikes, S'Albufera des Grau Natural Park UNESCO Biosphere 8 km north, and 24-hour vet emergency cover at Clínica Veterinaria Cardona & von Hofe (608 53 43 43).

name: Malaga
intro: Malaga combines a sunny Mediterranean climate with a relaxed attitude toward dogs: ideal for a beach-and-city break with your pet.

name: Malmö
intro: Malmö is southern Sweden's coastal hub - compact, walkable, with 61 enclosed dog parks, a year-round dog beach at Ribersborg, and free public transport for pets.

name: Manchester
intro: Manchester is among the UK's most dog-friendly cities: free pets on the Metrolink and Bee Network, dog-welcoming pubs on every Northern Quarter street, the 240-hectare Heaton Park a tram ride from the centre, and Vets Now's 24-hour hospital in Whitefield.

name: Marbella
intro: Marbella pairs the Costa del Sol's mildest year-round climate with two official dog beaches, a 7 km seafront promenade, and a whitewashed old town built for shaded strolls - one of southern Spain's most pet-comfortable destinations.

name: Marseille
intro: Marseille offers unrivalled outdoor pet travel with the Calanques National Park, Frioul island beaches accessible by ferry, and a Vieux-Port terrace scene that welcomes dogs throughout the year.

name: Matera
intro: Matera is a 60 000-resident UNESCO World Heritage city in Basilicata, southern Italy, built into the limestone ravine of the Gravina river around the Sassi cave dwellings of Sasso Caveoso and Sasso Barisano, inhabited continuously since the Paleolithic and named European Capital of Culture 2019. The rupestrian rock churches of Madonna de Idris, Santa Lucia alle Malve and San Pietro Caveoso, the Cattedrale on the highest tufa spur, the Piano upper town with Piazza Vittorio Veneto and the underground Palombaro Lungo cistern, and the 8 000 hectare Parco della Murgia Materana across the Gravina with 150+ rupestrian chapels and the Belvedere Murgia Timone film panorama (The Passion of the Christ, No Time to Die) anchor the dog-walkable heritage core. The FAL train from Bari Centrale (1h15-1h30) accepts dogs free of charge, the Pugliairbus shuttle links Bari BRI airport in 1h15, and Marozzi coaches reach Rome and Naples.

name: Menton
intro: Menton is the easternmost town on the French Côte d'Azur, ten minutes from the Italian border, with the warmest microclimate on mainland France, a Baroque old town climbing to the Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange, the historic Jardin Serre de la Madone and Jardin du Val Rahmeh which both admit leashed dogs, the Sentier Le Corbusier coastal path around Cap Martin, and a year-round IGP Citron de Menton lemon culture culminating in the February Fête du Citron. Direct TER trains connect to Nice (35 min), Monaco (10 min), and Ventimiglia in Italy (10 min); the nearest airport is Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE), 30 minutes by car or TER. Beach access for dogs runs October to mid-May; outdoor terrace dining is viable nearly year-round.

name: Miami
intro: Miami is Florida's South Beach Art Deco capital, where Ocean Drive's pastel hotel facades, the Lincoln Road pedestrian mall, the Wynwood Walls outdoor mural district, Brickell's waterfront skyline, Little Havana's Calle Ocho, Coconut Grove's bayfront promenade, Coral Gables' Mediterranean Revival villas and the Vizcaya gardens anchor a year-round outdoor lifestyle uniquely friendly to dogs. Two designated off-leash beaches (Hobie Island on the Rickenbacker Causeway and Haulover Dog Beach in Sunny Isles) plus large fenced dog parks at South Pointe, Margaret Pace, Tropical Park and Amelia Earhart give travellers genuine off-leash options. The Brightline intercity rail accepts pets up to 25 lb on every train, MIA airport is a CDC-approved dog-import gateway with two indoor pet relief areas, the Metromover and Metrobus admit small pets in carriers, and 24/7 emergency vet care is available across the metro. Peak season runs November to April; May to October brings 50-55 °C asphalt heat that limits midday walking.

name: Milan
intro: Milan is Italy's style capital and increasingly one of its most pet-welcoming cities: boutique hotels in the Navigli and Brera districts actively court guests with dogs. Parco Sempione, a 47-hectare green lung right beside the Castello Sforzesco, is perfect for morning walks before a day of exploring.

name: Modena
intro: Emilia-Romagna's gastronomic heart and home of balsamic vinegar, Ferrari, Maserati, Pavarotti. The Cathedral, Ghirlandina tower and Piazza Grande form a UNESCO World Heritage trio (1997). Compact and flat, easy walking with a dog. 35 min from Bologna and 1h45 from Milan by train. Spring and autumn are ideal; summers are humid (32°C), winters foggy.

name: Montpellier
intro: Montpellier's sun-soaked terraces, tram-laced streets, and the Grand Travers beach nearby make it one of southern France's most pet-welcoming cities for a city break.

name: Montreux
intro: Montreux on the Swiss Riviera blends Lake Geneva palms, the Château de Chillon, the Lavaux UNESCO vineyards, and the Quais Fleuris promenade where leashed dogs are welcome from Vevey to Villeneuve.

name: Munich
intro: Munich's English Garden, beer garden culture (dogs welcome), and excellent hotels make it ideal for a city break with your pet.

name: Nantes
intro: France’s most liveable city has ten dog parks (caniparcs), a QUALIDOG restaurant network, and a 12 km dog-friendly cultural trail, making it one of the most welcoming destinations in Europe for travelling with a pet.

name: Naples
intro: Italy's chaotic, passionate southern capital, gateway to Pompeii, Vesuvius, Capri and the Amalfi Coast. Dense historic-centre alleys, seafront Lungomare, 134 hectares of Bosco di Capodimonte, and pet-welcoming trattorie make it a rewarding (if demanding) stop for dog owners.

name: Narbonne
intro: Narbonne is a 55 000-resident Languedoc-Roussillon city with the unfinished Gothic Cathédrale Saint-Just, the Via Domitia Roman road, the UNESCO Canal de la Robine through the historic centre, Les Halles covered market, the 17 000-hectare Massif de la Clape garrigue, and a 15 km Mediterranean sand corridor 15 minutes east anchored by the year-round off-leash Saint-Pierre-la-Mer plage canine at Fleury-d'Aude (postal 11560).

name: Nazaré
intro: Nazaré, Portugal's Atlantic fishing town turned big-wave capital, pairs the clifftop Sítio quarter and Forte de São Miguel Arcanjo with the world-famous Praia do Norte canyon swells, a vintage funicular linking upper and lower town, and a long sandy beach where dogs are welcome outside the lifeguarded zone in summer.

name: Neringa
intro: Neringa is the UNESCO Curonian Spit resort municipality of four small lagoon villages (Nida, Juodkrante, Preila, Pervalka) on a 52 km sand spit reached only by ferry from Klaipeda, where leashed dogs roam pine-forest trails, the Parnidis sundial dune and the Nida lagoon promenade.

name: New York
intro: The first US destination on the site: Manhattan's skyline, 70+ dog runs, 24/7 emergency vets, and the most generous urban off-leash hours in America (5–9 am, 9 pm–1 am in Central and Prospect Parks). Dense, demanding in summer heat, and rewarding for travellers who want a pet-friendly city break beyond Europe.

name: Nice
intro: Nice's Mediterranean climate, Promenade des Anglais, and abundance of terrace restaurants make it a superb destination for pets year-round.

name: Nîmes
intro: Nîmes is the third corner of the Provence Roman triangle (with Avignon and Arles): the best-preserved Roman amphitheatre in the world, the UNESCO Maison Carrée, the 15-hectare Jardins de la Fontaine and the Pont du Gard 25 km north. The Arènes carry the Qualidog label and admit leashed dogs of all sizes free of charge, a French rarity.

name: Nuremberg
intro: Bavaria's second city and one of medieval Europe's great free imperial centres. The Kaiserburg castle, half-timbered Altstadt, and Albrecht Dürer's house anchor a compact UNESCO Tentative-listed core. Famous for its Christkindlesmarkt (Christmas market, since 1628), Lebkuchen gingerbread and Rostbratwurst. 1h05 from Munich and 4h from Berlin by ICE. Spring and autumn are ideal; winters cold but festive.

name: Oslo
intro: Oslo sits at the intersection of city life and wild nature, making it arguably Scandinavia's best city for dogs: fjords, forests, and snow-covered trails are all reachable by public transport. Hotels here routinely provide dog beds and bowls, and the expansive Nordmarka forest starts just 20 minutes from the centre.

name: Oxford
intro: England's medieval university city, honey-coloured college quadrangles, the 162-hectare off-lead Port Meadow, the Christ Church Meadow loop and the Thames towpath. Compact, walkable, with one of the country's highest pub dog-welcome rates and 24/7 emergency vet cover at Medivet Woodstock.

name: Padua
intro: Veneto's UNESCO-listed university city, anchored by Europe's largest square Prato della Valle (88,620 m²), 25+ km of porticoed arcades, off-leash aree cani in every district and a fixed €5 Trenitalia fare to Venice or Verona in under 40 minutes. Compact, walkable and one of Italy's quietest dog-friendly cultural bases.

name: Palermo
intro: Sicily's vibrant capital (~660k inhabitants), gateway to Sicilian beaches and the Mediterranean's chaotic-baroque heart. The Arab-Norman UNESCO ensemble (Cathedral, Royal Palace's Capella Palatina, Zisa) layers nine centuries of Mediterranean rule. Vucciria + Ballarò markets, the Foro Italico seafront, Mondello dog-beach 11 km north. 1h flight from Rome, ferry hub to Tunis and Naples. Sicilian taverna culture is unusually dog-friendly on terraces.

name: Pamplona
intro: Capital of Navarra in Northern Spain, Hemingway's favourite city, world-famous for the San Fermines bull-running festival (6-14 July). ~205k inhabitants, walled medieval old town, the Citadel park (Ciudadela, 280k m²), and the Camino de Santiago French route runs straight through the centre. 1h45 from Madrid by Renfe AVE, 1h from Bilbao by Alsa bus. One of Spain's most dog-positive cities, pintxo bar culture welcomes dogs on terraces year-round.

name: Paris
intro: Paris welcomes pets in many hotels, cafés, and even some restaurants.

name: Perpignan
intro: Perpignan, the sunny Catalan capital of the French south, is a compact and genuinely dog-friendly city with around 37 marked dog areas, a tolerant terrace culture, a 24-hour emergency vet, and easy access to the dog-friendly Roussillon beaches of Canet-en-Roussillon and Torreilles.

name: Piran
intro: Piran, Slovenia's Venetian jewel on the Adriatic Riviera, packs Tartini Square, the San Giorgio bell tower, the medieval Walls of Piran and a car-free old town into a stone peninsula ringed by pet-friendly seafront terraces, with Monty's Dog Beach at Lucija, the Strunjan flysch cliffs and the Sečovlje salt pans within easy reach.

name: Pisa
intro: Pisa pairs a compact UNESCO Old Town with the 23,000-hectare Migliarino San Rossore park and the dog-friendly Tyrrhenian coast at Marina di Pisa, all reachable by city bus. The University Veterinary Hospital adds a 24-hour safety net.

name: Porto
intro: Porto's hilly streets, river esplanades, and laid-back attitude make it one of Portugal's most welcoming cities for travelling with a dog.

name: Poznan
intro: Poznan is the cradle of the Polish state, founded in 966 around the Cathedral Island where the first Polish king Mieszko I was baptised. The colourful Stary Rynek (Old Market Square) is one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, with the famous mechanical goats butting heads on the Town Hall at noon. Beyond the centre, the 64-hectare Lake Malta with its city beach, the Citadel Park's panoramic terrace, and the Wielkopolska National Park 30 km south make Poznan a quiet pet-travel favourite. Trams accept dogs with a single ticket, around forty fenced off-leash zones are scattered across the city, and the cafe terraces around the Rynek welcome leashed dogs without fuss.

name: Prague
intro: Prague's compact old town and riverside parks make it an underrated gem for travelling with dogs.

name: Pula
intro: Istria`s 53,000-resident former Roman capital on the southern tip of the peninsula, anchored by the 1st-century Arena (one of the six best-preserved Roman amphitheatres in the world), the Forum with its Augustan Temple of Augustus, the Arch of the Sergii and the Kaštel fortress hilltop, with the Punta Verudela peninsula 4 km south and the off-leash Cape Kamenjak nature park 10 km further on, plus PUY airport 7 km out, a regional rail link to Slovenia and the seasonal Venezia Lines catamaran to Italy.

name: Regensburg
intro: A 155,000-resident Bavarian city on the Danube where one of Europe's best-preserved medieval Altstadts (UNESCO since 2006) is fully walkable in 30 minutes with a dog. The 12th-century Steinerne Brücke, the Gothic cathedral of St Peter, the riverside Spitalgarten beer garden and the Walhalla terraces above the Danube anchor a calm, dog-tolerant atmosphere far less crowded than Munich or Nuremberg.

name: Reims
intro: Reims, the coronation city of French kings and the capital of Champagne, combines the UNESCO Notre-Dame Cathedral (33 kings crowned), the Palais du Tau, the Pommery cellar gardens, and direct TGV access from Paris Gare de l'Est in 45 minutes.

name: Rennes
intro: Rennes, capital of Brittany, blends the half-timbered medieval centre rebuilt after the 1720 fire, the 10-hectare Parc du Thabor, France's second-largest Saturday market on Place des Lices, and day-trip access to Saint-Malo and the Côte d'Émeraude, making it one of north-west France's most walkable pet-friendly bases.

name: Reykjavik
intro: Reykjavik's clean air, dramatic landscapes, and dog-welcoming culture make it a unique and increasingly popular destination for adventurous pet owners.

name: Riga
intro: Riga's Art Nouveau architecture, riverside parks, and affordable hotels make it an emerging gem for pet-friendly city breaks in the Baltics.

name: Rimini
intro: Rimini is the capital of Italy's Adriatic Riviera and one of the country's best beach destinations for dog owners, home to Rimini Dog No Problem (the largest dedicated dog beach on the Emilia-Romagna coast), a fenced off-leash park along the Marecchia river, two 24-hour vets, and a Roman and Renaissance old town that is easy to explore on a leash.

name: Rome
intro: Rome combines ancient grandeur with a surprisingly relaxed attitude toward pets: dogs are welcome in many piazzas, parks, and hotel terraces.

name: Rotterdam
intro: Rotterdam is one of Europe's most dog-friendly cities, with free public transport for pets, five off-leash parks, and a vibrant café culture that welcomes dogs by default.

name: Rovinj
intro: Istria`s Venetian jewel on the Adriatic west coast, a former islet of pastel houses tumbling down to the harbour under the 60 m belltower of sv. Eufemije, with the 300-acre Punta Corrente forest park and four signposted dog beaches (Plaža Cisterna at Lone Bay, Plaža Borik, Plaža Mulini, Plaža Škaraba), a bilingual Croatian-Italian Stari Grad, the seasonal Venezia Lines catamaran to Venezia, and one of the most genuinely pet-friendly small towns on the eastern Adriatic.

name: Saint-Tropez
intro: Saint-Tropez is a 4,000-resident Provençal harbour town on the western Côte d'Azur, defined by its working Vieux Port, the 16th-century Citadelle, the plane-tree-shaded Place des Lices market (Tuesday and Saturday), the 5 km Pampelonne beach sweep in neighbouring Ramatuelle, and the 35 km Sentier du Littoral coastal path around the peninsula. The town has no SNCF station: the nearest rail head is Saint-Raphaël-Valescure 45 km away, linked year-round by Var-Lib bus 7601 (90 min) or seasonally by Bateaux de Saint-Raphaël ferry (50 min); the Bateaux Verts crossing from Sainte-Maxime takes 15 minutes. The two regional airports are Toulon-Hyères (TLN, 1 h) and Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE, 1 h 15). Beach access for dogs runs October to mid-May; rosé-fuelled terrace dining is reliable from May to October.

name: Salamanca
intro: Castile's golden sandstone university city, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988. Compact and walkable: the Plaza Mayor (one of Spain's finest), the twin cathedrals, and the Roman Bridge over the Tormes river. 1.5h by AVE from Madrid. Dogs roam easily through arcaded streets and the Salas Bajas riverside parks. Spring and autumn are ideal; summer hits 35°C, winter brings cold dry nights.

name: Salzburg
intro: Salzburg's compact baroque centre and the dramatic Alpine scenery surrounding it create an unforgettable backdrop for travelling with pets. The Mirabell Gardens and the footpaths ascending to the Hohensalzburg fortress are both dog-friendly, and hotels here often provide pet amenities.

name: San Francisco
intro: San Francisco is the cool, foggy Pacific gateway to the Bay Area, where ~30 fenced Rec & Park Dog Play Areas plus the federal GGNRA off-leash sections (Crissy Field East Beach with the Golden Gate Bridge view, Fort Funston bluffs and beach, Ocean Beach north of Stairwell 21) make it one of the densest off-leash networks in the US. Golden Gate Park's Hellman Hollow and Speedway Meadow DPAs anchor the 412-hectare flagship park, Lands End coastal trail leads to the Sutro Baths ruins, and the Presidio's forest paths overlook the Bay. BART, Muni Metro/bus and cable car all accept small pets in carriers free; the Golden Gate Ferry to Sausalito takes leashed dogs free on the outer deck; SFO is a CDC-approved international dog-arrival airport with indoor pet relief areas. Three 24/7 emergency vets (SAGE Mission, SFAMC Fillmore, VEG Greenbrae) cover the metro. Cool fog summers (10-15 °C) and dry sunny fall make it walkable year-round; the only constraints are the hilly streets and the cold Pacific rip currents on the ocean side.

name: San Sebastián
intro: San Sebastián (Donostia) has more registered dogs per inhabitant than any other major Spanish city, and it shows, Michelin-starred restaurants welcome dogs without hesitation, Monte Urgull offers vast off-leash hillside walks, and La Concha's crescent beach opens to dogs every October for a full six months.

name: Sankt Pölten
intro: Lower Austria's quiet capital, a 56,000-resident city on the Traisen river with a pedestrian Baroque Altstadt, the modernist Government Quarter and Klangturm tower, and the Wachau wine villages of Dürnstein, Spitz and Krems all within 45 minutes. Vienna is 25 minutes by Railjet.

name: Sant Antoni de Portmany
intro: The 28,000-resident western capital of Ibiza, world-famous for the Sunset Strip clifftop bars and the Cafe del Mar mixtape tradition since 1980, the 14th-century Església de Sant Antoni de Portmany (the oldest church on Ibiza), Hostal La Torre and Punta Galera for quieter sunsets, white-sand Cala Bassa, sunset-facing Cala Conta and family-friendly Cala Tarida on the west coast, Es Vedrà boat excursions, and a Baleària fast ferry from the Port Deportiu to Dénia on the Spanish mainland (2h45) with pet cabins on the Eleanor Roosevelt. Ibiza Airport (IBZ) 15 km south-east by taxi or TIB L8 bus.

name: Sant Josep de sa Talaia
intro: Largest municipality on Ibiza by area, 28,000 residents covering the entire south of the island: Es Vedrà (the 382 m vertical limestone monolith offshore from Cala d'Hort, with its 'third most magnetic place on Earth' lore), Sa Talaia (the island's 475 m highest peak, 2 h round-trip hike from the village), the 18th-century Església de Sant Josep in the casco antiguo plaza, the Parque Natural de Ses Salines d'Eivissa i Formentera (UNESCO Biosphere with salt pans, flamingos and Posidonia seagrass meadow), and the Sa Pedrera (Atlantis) quarry-cove descent. Beaches from Cala d'Hort, Cala Vadella, Cala Tarida, Cala Molí and Cala Carbó on the south-west to Cala Jondal, Sa Caleta, Es Codolar and the 2.7 km Platja d'en Bossa club strip on the south. Ibiza Airport (IBZ) sits inside the municipality 2 km from Platja d'en Bossa; TIB buses L24/L21/L25/L26 cover the area, no rail or ferry port, Aquabus seasonal coastal boats for summer cove-hopping, Es Vedrà boat tours from Cala d'Hort.

name: Santa Eulària des Riu
intro: Calmer family resort on Ibiza's east coast (38,000 year-round residents), wrapped around the whitewashed 16th-century church-fortress of Puig de Missa, the Riu de Santa Eulària (the only year-round river in the Pitiüses) with its Pont Vell Roman bridge and mil de baix windmill, a long Paseo Marítimo and Marina, and the Saturday Las Dalias hippie market in Sant Carles. Year-round dog beach at Cala Nova (north of Es Canar), shoulder-season tolerance at Cala Llonga and Cala Pada, and Ibiza Airport (IBZ) 22 km south-west by taxi or TIB L18 bus.

name: Santander
intro: Cantabria's bayside capital pairs the Belle Époque crescent of El Sardinero and the royal Magdalena peninsula with a year-round Brittany Ferries link to Plymouth and Portsmouth, a dedicated off-leash zone at Parque de las Llamas and a 24/7 veterinary hospital on Avenida de los Castros, the most practical Cantabrian Sea city for a dog-inclusive trip.

name: Santiago de Compostela
intro: Galicia's UNESCO-listed pilgrim capital with granite-paved squares around the cathedral, six designated off-leash dog spaces, a 24/7 reference vet hospital at Costa Vella, and a municipal 'Santiguau' programme formally listing pet-friendly venues across the old town.

name: Santorini
intro: Santorini (Thira, ~15k year-round residents, 76 km² Cycladic volcanic island) is a crescent-shaped caldera with the whitewashed cliff-top villages of Fira (capital), Firostefani, Imerovigli and Oia draped along the 300 m caldera rim. The 10 km clifftop caldera path from Fira to Oia is the signature dog walk (dawn or after 17:00, paws burn at midday), the hilltop villages of Pyrgos and Megalochori offer calmer Cycladic atmosphere away from the summer crush, and the Akrotiri Bronze Age Minoan site under its bioclimatic roof is the headline archaeology. Beaches are volcanic: Red Beach (Akrotiri), 7 km Black Beach Perissa/Perivolos, Vlychada under lunar bluffs, the boat-access White Beach. JTR airport sits 6 km southeast of Fira (year-round Aegean/SKY Express to Athens, summer EU charters), Athinios port runs Blue Star and Sea Jets ferries from Piraeus (5-8h) plus inter-island catamarans. Not a budget pet destination: hotels charge 20-40 EUR/night pet supplement, July-August sees 50k+ daily tourists and asphalt hits 50-60 °C. Apr-May and October are the dog-friendly windows.

name: Sète
intro: Sète is a 44 000-resident Hérault port city built on the slopes of Mont Saint-Clair between the Mediterranean and the Étang de Thau oyster lagoon, nicknamed the Venice of Languedoc for its working canal grid. Highlights include the 175 m Mont Saint-Clair panoramic terrace, the Cimetière Marin where Paul Valéry rests, the 12 km Plage de la Corniche with the year-round off-leash Lazaret plage canine, and the dog-friendly Sète-Mèze ferry across the Étang de Thau to the Bouzigues oyster villages.

name: Setúbal
intro: Setúbal is a working Atlantic port wrapped around the Sado estuary, with translucent Arrábida coves 15 minutes from the centre, a year-round dolphin ferry to the Tróia peninsula, the 110 km² Serra da Arrábida Natural Park rising directly from the sea, and an underrated tasca culture built around choco frito and Moscatel. 24/7 vet cover and an easy 50-minute Fertagus train to central Lisbon anchor every itinerary.

name: Seville
intro: Seville's orange-tree lined streets, riverside promenades, and vibrant terrace culture make it one of Andalusia's most dog-friendly cities.

name: Siena
intro: Siena is a 53 000-resident UNESCO World Heritage hilltop city in southern Tuscany, built around the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo and divided into 17 contrade (medieval neighborhoods) that compete in the Palio horse race on 2 July and 16 August. The white-and-black marble striped Duomo Cathedral, the 14th-century Palazzo Pubblico, the 102 m Torre del Mangia, the Fortezza Medicea panoramic ramparts, the Orto de' Pecci medieval valley garden and the Via Francigena pilgrim route through Porta Camollia and Porta Romana anchor the walled centre. Trenitalia regional Florence-Siena (1h15-1h45) accepts muzzled dogs, Tiemme/Sena buses link San Gimignano, Volterra, Montepulciano and the Crete Senesi rolling hills, and Florence FLR airport is 70 km north via direct 90 min Autostradale coach.

name: Sintra
intro: Sintra, the UNESCO Cultural Landscape 30 minutes from Lisbon, combines polychrome Romantic palaces in the Serra de Sintra, the botanical gardens of Pena, Regaleira and Monserrate, kilometres of leashy laurel-forest trails, the dramatic Atlantic cliffs of Cabo da Roca and a mild oceanic climate that stays pet-friendly year-round.

name: Sitges
intro: Sitges is a 30,000-resident Catalan seaside town 35 km south-west of Barcelona, with 17 beaches stretched over 3.5 km of the Costa del Garraf, a designated dog beach at Platja de la Bassa Rodona during the August-September window, the traditionally tolerant Platja dels Balmins cove, the cliff-top Església de Sant Bartomeu i Santa Tecla baroque silhouette, the Casc Antic cobbles around the Palau Maricel and Museu del Cau Ferrat, the Parc de Terramar gardens, the Parc Natural del Garraf hinterland, and a 24/7 reference vet hospital on Ctra. de Pruelles. Rodalies R2 Sud from Barcelona-Sants reaches Sitges in 35 minutes, Mon-Bus runs a 30-minute shuttle from Barcelona-El Prat (BCN) airport, and the city anchors one of Europe`s most settled LGBT travel scenes around Carnaval (February), Bears Sitges Week (September) and the Fantastic Film Festival (October).

name: Sofia
intro: Sofia is one of the EU's most affordable capitals: nearly 500 dog-friendly venues, two 24/7 emergency vet hospitals, and the 2,290 m Vitosha mountain rising directly from the city, all reachable on foot or one metro ride.

name: Sóller
intro: Sóller is a 14k orange-valley town in Mallorca's UNESCO Serra de Tramuntana, reached from Palma by the 1912 wooden Ferrocarril and from the natural horseshoe Port de Sóller by the 1913 open-air Tranvía vintage tram. Modernist Plaça d'Espanya, the GR-221 Ruta de Pedra en Sec dry-stone trail, the Pinos boat to Sa Calobra, Cap Gros lighthouse views, and naranjas + oli Sóller PDO make it Mallorca's most genuinely pet-friendly mountain base.

name: Sorrento
intro: Sorrento is a 16 000-resident Campania cliff town in the Metropolitan City of Naples and the gateway hub for the Amalfi Coast, Capri, Ischia and Pompeii, hosting roughly 3 million tourists a year. The historic Piazza Tasso anchors the centro storico, the panoramic Villa Comunale gardens look 80 m down onto the Marina Grande old fishing port, the Marina Piccola ferry terminal runs 30+ daily SNAV/Caremar/NLG hydrofoils to Capri (25 min), Ischia (50 min) and Naples (35 min), the EAV Circumvesuviana uniquely accepts muzzled dogs free of charge for the direct 35 min trip to Pompei Scavi, and the SITA SUD Amalfi Coast bus links Positano (50 min), Amalfi (1h30) and the Path of the Gods trailhead at Bomerano.

name: Split
intro: Split's Adriatic setting delivers the perfect combination for pet owners: a gorgeous coastline, a compact walkable old town, and an increasingly pet-friendly hospitality scene. The seaside Riva promenade and the green Marjan Hill forest park: essentially a dog-walker's paradise: are both within a short stroll.

name: Stavanger
intro: Stavanger, Norway's third city and the gateway to the Lysefjord, combines a UNESCO-rated wooden Old Town (Gamle Stavanger), exceptionally dog-friendly transport (free buses, free trains, free fjord ferries), the iconic Pulpit Rock 50 min east, and 35 km of dog-friendly Atlantic sand 15 min south.

name: Stockholm
intro: Stockholm's archipelago setting, vast green spaces, and dog-welcoming culture make it one of Scandinavia's best cities for pet travel.

name: Stuttgart
intro: Stuttgart sits in a green basin ringed by vineyards and beech forests, a southern German capital where Biergärten and Wirtschaften universally welcome dogs, the Schlossgarten ribbon links the centre to the Neckar, and the Bärensee forest reservoirs offer cool summer walks twenty minutes from the centre.

name: Tallinn
intro: Tallinn's beautifully preserved medieval old town, coastal paths, and dog-friendly hotels make it a hidden gem for pet travel in Northern Europe.

name: Tampere
intro: Tampere, Finland's third city and the unofficial sauna capital, combines a compact lake-bordered centre, exceptionally dog-friendly transport (free trams, free trains), 22 fenced koira-aitaus, two lake dog beaches and direct rail access from Helsinki in 1h30.

name: Tarifa
intro: Tarifa, the southernmost point of mainland Europe on the Strait of Gibraltar, is a tiny medieval town that doubles as the kitesurf and windsurf capital of the world. Ten kilometres of flat-sand Playa de Los Lances open to leashed dogs out of season, the Roman ruins of Baelo Claudia behind dog-friendly Bolonia beach, a 35-minute FRS ferry to Tangier, and a 24-hour vet on-call line make it one of southern Spain`s most distinctive small-town bases for pet travel.

name: Tarragona
intro: Tarragona, Catalonia's UNESCO-listed Roman seaport on the Costa Daurada, pairs an open-air 2nd-century amphitheatre with three designated dog beaches (Platja Llarga, Platja del Miracle and Bon Caponet), the wild pine-forest cove of Cala Fonda, and 24/7 referral vet care 5 km away at AniCura Bofarull. Renfe Rodalies trains carry leashed dogs to Barcelona in 70 minutes.

name: Tavira
intro: Tavira, the quieter eastern Algarve town split by the Rio Gilão and its seven-arch Ponte Romana, opens onto the Parque Natural da Ria Formosa, the year-round Ilha de Tavira ferry from Quatro Águas (5-min crossing), the Praia do Barril mini-train and anchor cemetery, the Cabanas de Tavira sandbar, and the Cacela Velha clifftop village. The CP Linha do Algarve and Vamus EVA coastal buses run east to the Vila Real de Santo António ferry crossing the Rio Guadiana to Ayamonte in Spain.

name: Texel
intro: Texel is the Netherlands' most painlessly dog-friendly Wadden island: a 24 km long North Sea spit 20 minutes by TESO ferry from Den Helder (dogs cross free), with five year-round off-leash dog beaches (Paal 8 Mokbaai, Paal 9 Den Hoorn, Paal 17 De Koog, Paal 28 and Paal 31 at the Eierland lighthouse), the 4,300-hectare Nationaal Park Duinen van Texel running almost the full western dune belt, and the 850-hectare De Dennen pine forest in the centre with year-round off-leash loops. Seven villages share the island culture (Den Burg as the cobbled capital, De Koog beside the dog beach pavilions, Oudeschild with the working fishing harbour and the Texelse Bierbrouwerij, Den Hoorn around its 1,500-resident square, De Cocksdorp at the lighthouse, plus Oosterend and De Waal). The De Slufter salt marsh and Wagejot mudflats on the east coast are NATURA 2000 reserves (eastern Wadden Sea coast closed to dogs year-round for bird protection). Texelhopper buses serve every village and dune entry, dogs ride free. From Schiphol Airport the door-to-ferry trip is about 1h45 by car.

name: The Hague
intro: The Hague pairs Dutch political grandeur with a 11-kilometre North Sea coastline, off-leash dunes a tram ride from the centre, and dog-friendly cafés on every corner of the Statenkwartier and Scheveningen Haven.

name: Toledo
